sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar continues that the miracle of "that night the king's sleep fled" was caused by Israel's self-sacrifice throughout the year, yet this raises questions about why such a miracle was needed when Israel was doing God's will.

translations.translation: And the maamar continues,
that this — that on that night the sleep of the King, the King of the world, fled
(the essential miracle of Purim)
was brought about by the self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh) of Israel throughout the entire year.
And it needs to be understood:
Behold, at the time when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent,
then
(according to the order of the chain of descent)
He does
not slumber nor sleep.
And since Israel stood in self-sacrifice throughout the entire year,
what is the miracle, and moreover the intensity
of the miracle, in that the King's sleep fled?
Also, it needs to be understood:
For the simple meaning of "on that night the king's sleep fled" refers to King Achashverosh,
it is
that the things that occurred on that night caused the king's sleep to flee.
And according to the known principle that matters below descend from their counterpart above,
it is understood
that likewise, regarding this — that the sleep of the King, the King of the world, fled —
the matter of "that night" is what caused the King's sleep to flee.
And it needs to be understood:
Behold, "that night" indicates
(as above, section 1)
concealment and hiding and their magnitude,
the opposite of the concept that "that night" brings about the fleeing of the sleep of the King, the King of the world.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This is understood by prefacing the explanation in Torah Or and the Mitteler Rebbe's discourse that both day and night have aspects of revelation and concealment, indicated by the terms "this" and "that."

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing what is explained in Torah Or in the discourses of Purim,
and at length in the discourse of the Mitteler Rebbe,
that in "day"
(revelation)
and in "night"
(concealment),
in each of them,
there are two aspects: revelation and concealment.
And this is why sometimes it is written "this day" (hayom hazeh),
which indicates revelation,
and sometimes it is written "that day" (hayom hahu),
which indicates concealment
(as above),
and likewise regarding night, sometimes it is written "this night" and sometimes "that night."
And the point of the explanation
(as understood from the discourses)
is that the difference between day and night is in themselves,
for day is light and night is darkness, as it is written,
"And God called the light day, and the darkness He called night."
And there is another difference in the manner of day and night,
whether they are in a manner of revelation
("zeh" — this)
or in a manner of concealment
("hu" — that).
For the term "zeh" regarding day and night indicates the day and night as they are drawn down below in revelation,
and the term "hu" indicates the day and night as they are in their essence
(before they are drawn down in revelation),
and even higher — as they are in their root.
And this is why regarding the redemption from Egypt it is written,
"On this very day (etzem hayom hazeh), all the hosts of Hashem went out of the land of Egypt,"
and likewise regarding the giving of the Torah
(as it is now)
it is written,
"This day (hayom hazeh) Hashem your God commands you...,"
and regarding the future redemption it is written,
"And it shall be said on that day (bayom hahu)...."
For the revelation that was in the redemption from Egypt is the revelation of the light as it is drawn down below,
"this day,"
and in the future redemption there will be a revelation of the essence of the light as it is above drawing down and revelation,
"that day."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Similarly regarding night, the darkness that is above light is called "that night," and when drawn down it is called "this night," yet "that night" is a greater darkness than "this night."

translations.translation: And likewise regarding night,
the aspect of darkness that is above light
(above even the essence of light),
the darkness itself before it is drawn down in revelation
(and all the more so as it is in its root)
is called "that night" (leil hahu),
and when it is drawn down below it is called "this night" (leil hazeh).
However, regarding night,
"that night" is lower than "this night."
For since the darkness of night that is above light is the root and cause through which simple darkness is brought about,
therefore the concealment and hiding
(simple darkness)
that is brought about by the drawing down of the essence of darkness
(which is above),
"that night,"
is a greater darkness than the darkness brought about by the drawing down of darkness as it comes in a drawn-down manner,
"this night."
For "this night" is that the night is in a manner of "this,"
that it is felt in revelation
[to the extent of revelation that one can point with a finger and say "this"]
that it is night,
and "that night" is that the night is in a manner of concealment
that it is not felt that it is night.
